label: sec:molecular-chains-rings-intro
html:
Atoms are assembled into extended molecular structures.

This section reads off the dynamical consequences. Open chains behave as topological springs. Ring closure is a topological phase transition. The transition state is the barrier where pairwise bonds dissolve before the threading link forms. The same mechanism explains ring super-stability. As in the preceding chapter, these Hopf chains and threading links are algebraic operators in H_n(q) representing covalent delocalisation, distinct from the spatial molecular knots and catenanes of topological stereochemistry [dietrich-buchecker-sauvage1989, flapan2000].
